subject.title: Reply-session init conflict is silently dropped on Slack/webchat/heartbeat inbound, though Telegram already treats it as retryable

question: Should this issue be resolved by landing the shared reply-session self-heal in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920, or by adding per-inbound retry/coalescing to the remaining affected surfaces?
rationale: Both approaches can address message loss, but they have different session-state and delivery-risk profiles, and an open proof-positive pull request already owns the shared recovery path.

options.title: Review and land shared self-heal
options.body: Use the open self-heal pull request as the canonical fix if its session-state and message-delivery risks are acceptable after maintainer review.

options.title: Require surface-specific retry parity
options.body: Keep the source throw behavior and add explicit retry/coalescing only to webchat, heartbeat, and any remaining channel adapters.

options.title: Pause for more live evidence
options.body: Keep the issue open without new repair work until maintainers decide the open pull request’s proof is not enough for the shared lifecycle change.

recommendation.title: Review and land shared self-heal
recommendation.body: Use the open self-heal pull request as the canonical fix if its session-state and message-delivery risks are acceptable after maintainer review.

likelyOwner.reason: The current core session, heartbeat, and webchat paths in this review route through code recently attributed to this area contributor in local history.
